Free to go further

A fare should never decide whether a young person reaches a job, a college, a clinic or a friend.

Become a memberBecome an ambassadorSee the evidence

The campaign

Free public transport for every young person under 22

Scotland has shown what free travel does. We are asking for one national scheme so that a boundary no longer sets the fare.

The evidence

What the numbers say

These figures come from the Free to Go Further report, which lists every source.

981,000

people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training in April to June 2026.

+94%

rise in bus fares between 2015 and 2025, more than twice the rise in prices overall.

250m+

free bus journeys made by under-22s in Scotland since January 2022.

49p

a day is what Scotland's scheme costs for each eligible young person.

51% to 20%

fall in the share of young Scots who said cost was a barrier to using the bus.

£1,195

is spent on transport per person in London, against £376 in the East Midlands.

32%

of people aged 17 to 20 hold a full driving licence, down from 48% in the early 1990s.

£2.87

is returned for each £1 spent on free bus travel for older and disabled people.

Become a regional ambassador

Speak up for transport where you live

Ambassadors are volunteers aged 18 or over. You will gather local stories, meet councillors and MPs, and represent your region in the campaign.

You must be 18 or over to apply.
Optional.
Up to 150 words. This may appear on your profile if you are appointed.

Become a member

Join the campaign

Membership is free. Members add their name to the call for free travel and receive our bi-monthly email with campaign news and ways to help. You do not need to be an ambassador to join.

Optional.
Optional.

Contact us

Get in touch

Write to us about the campaign, press enquiries, partnerships or a story from where you live.
